subject: Dedicated SKU wargame — H100/A100/L4 scenarios for Stratify Labs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Stratify request — need a SKU wargame

Team —

Stratify (Alex) pinged asking for an apples-to-apples set of deployment scenarios so their architects + procurement can choose a path for Dedicated. High level ask: three scenarios (cost-min / balanced / performance-first) with rough GPU counts, ops assumptions (cache, eviction headroom), and estimated monthly $/token run-rate. They want something they can take into procurement next week.

I started a spreadsheet and attached a baseline scenario sheet (stratify_gpu_scenarios.xlsx). Can each of you take a focused slice:
- Irene: hardware perf tradeoffs and memory headroom assumptions per SKU (H100 / A100 / L4).
- Ben: production tiling/batching implications and rough latency SLOs per scenario; ops friction (warmup, KV cache hit assumptions).
- Marissa: commercial framing — comms for procurement, pricing buckets and commitment tiers.

Goal: consolidate and send a customer-facing PDF by Mon 10/13 10am PDT. If you think we should run a short internal wargame (30m) tomorrow, reply with availability.

Thanks —
Jonas
Director, Solution Architecture
Redwood Inference

Attachment: stratify_gpu_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet, 420KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FW: Stratify request — need a SKU wargame

Jonas — quick notes from perf/infra POV after a first pass through the spreadsheet. Attaching a matrix with microbench numbers and memory headroom assumptions (latency_perf_matrix.csv).

High-level recommendations (short):
- L4: excellent cost per token for short-context inference and embedding-heavy workloads. Limited per-instance memory (24GB effective in our quantized L4 profile) — feasible as a baseline for token-only pipelines and high-QPS low-context paths. Expect cold-start variance ~10-20ms depending on concurrent slots.

- A100 (40GB): balanced option. Good for mid-length contexts (up to ~8k tokens with our multi-stage KV caching), better concurrency than L4 for moderate batch sizes. Lower single-token latency than H100 in some quantized runs, but less headroom for very long contexts. Use as primary compute for mixed workloads where 30-40% of requests are medium-length.

- H100 (80GB): memory-first, best for long-context and large batch troughs. Recommended when >10% of requests need >16k context or when serving large instruction-finetuned models requiring 40GB+ KV cache support. Higher cost per token but fewer fallbacks and simpler routing.

Notes on ops tradeoffs:
- Cache hit assumptions: assume 40% prefix reuse in their chat flows (they said many quick-followups). If that holds, A100 + L4 hybrid reduces unit cost significantly.
- Eviction headroom: reserve ~15% of slot memory for model metadata to avoid OOM in bursty workloads. This pushes recommended per-slot sizing up slightly.
- Fallback behavior: prefer 'A100 degrade to L4' for cost saves only if model quantization path validated; otherwise degrade to smaller H100 config or queue.

I'll propose concrete slot counts in the next message after Ben's latency view.

Irene
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency_perf_matrix.csv (CSV, 92KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratifylabs.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed customer-facing scenarios (draft)

Alex / Stratify team — looping you in so you have visibility. Below are three numbered scenarios we recommend for Dedicated. This is a draft for discussion — if you can confirm traffic shape we can tighten the numbers.

Scenario 1 — Cost-first (L4-centric)- Target: 95% short-context QPS (<=256 tokens), embeddings-heavy.- HW: L4-only pool, 128 slots (elastic), estimated 24 L4 instances (quantized profiles).- Ops: aggressive batching, KV caching minimal; expect median token latency in 25-40ms depending on concurrency.- Tradeoffs: Cannot support >8k contexts reliably; higher variance on cold starts.- Monthly run-rate (est): $Xk/mo (depends on commitments).

Scenario 2 — Balanced (A100 + L4 hybrid)- Target: mixed traffic: 55% short, 35% medium, 10% long.- HW: primary A100 pool (40GB) for medium/long paths + L4 for short-context scale. Suggested baseline: 10 A100 instances + 16 L4 instances (slotting + burst to A100 as needed).- Ops: prefix KV cache shared across A100 pool; auto-fallback rules to L4 for non-memory-bound requests.- Tradeoffs: Best unit economics for mixed workloads; moderate ops complexity.- Monthly run-rate (est): $Yk/mo.

Scenario 3 — Performance-first (H100-heavy)- Target: >10% very long-context requests, strict p95 latency SLOs.- HW: H100 pool (80GB) with conservative headroom. Suggested baseline: 6 H100 instances + 6 A100 for midworkload spill.- Ops: minimized cross-SKU routing, prioritized KV residency to avoid re-fetches.- Tradeoffs: Highest cost per token but simplifies routing and reduces quality regressions for long-context.- Monthly run-rate (est): $Zk/mo.

Next steps for Stratify: can you confirm 1) target sustained QPS and 2) percentage distribution across short/medium/long? Also, do you have an internal latency SLO? If procurement needs a short SOW, we can attach a 1-page technical appendix and a sample commitment table.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: stratify_sku_proposal.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@stratifylabs.com>

Cc: procurement@stratifylabs.com
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed customer-facing scenarios (draft)

Ben / Jonas / team — thanks, this is exactly the framing we need. A few clarifications and next steps from our side:

Traffic snapshot (last 30 days): sustained 220 qps average across APIs, peak 480 qps sustained for 30–45 minutes during business hours. Token distribution roughly: 70% short (<512), 20% medium (512–4k), 10% long (>4k). Latency SLO target: p95 < 300ms for interactive flows; for batch embedding paths p95 < 1s is fine.

We prefer Scenario 2 as our baseline but want a hedged pilot that includes a small H100 reserve for unexpectedly heavy long-context bursts. Proposed immediate ask:
- Pilot: 6 A100 + 12 L4 + 2 H100 reserved (warm but not primary).- Procurement to receive SOW + pricing table; copying procurement (procurement@stratifylabs.com) for contract coordination.

If you can produce a 1-page SOW and an itemized price table (commit tiers monthly / annual and burst pricing), we can start internal approvals. Also please include the operation assumptions (KV cache hit %, eviction headroom) you used for the numbers.

Happy to meet Wed 10/15 10am PT for a short technical alignment.

Alex Morgan
Head of Platform & Infrastructure
Stratify Labs
